identity.title: Bound MCP admission, request deadlines and reconnect recovery

closure_unit.outcome: The existing MCP owner bounds admitted requests and buffered bytes, settles every local request path, and rejects expired or revoked work before reconnect dispatch while response/cancellation handling remains available.

materialized_acceptance.text: Define one typed lifecycle for each admitted MCP request, including admission, queued, dispatched, cancellation requested, caller completed and remote settlement or unknown outcome. Bound accepted item count, encoded bytes, waiting producers and pending metadata before allocation. Resolve finite policy values through the existing owning configuration and record their source; do not invent unreviewed caps.

Replace unbounded transport and reconnect buffering with bounded admission and explicit overflow/backpressure outcomes across stdio, reconnect and duplex test seams. Reserve capacity for response, completion, cancellation and shutdown traffic. A slow or stalled inbound request/notification handler cannot prevent response matching, expiry, cancellation or transport control; extra tasks also remain bounded.

Every supported request class receives an absolute deadline at admission, including initialize/handshake, tools/list, resources/list, tools/call and server-originated handler work where supported. Queueing, permit waits, writing, reconnect and response waiting consume that same lifetime. Progress notifications cannot extend it silently. Apply protocol-valid initialization cancellation behavior; a deadline does not authorize an invalid notifications/cancelled message.

For send_request and send_request_with_id, failed admission or failed send removes the pending entry and releases its local permit exactly once. Dispatcher EOF, transport closure, exhausted reconnect and client shutdown settle every local waiter with a typed terminal reason; no unresolved oneshot or retained pending map survives unnoticed. Retain separate uncertainty accounting for dispatched remote work until MT-205 observes settlement.

Reconnect never dispatches a request that expired or was cancelled while disconnected. Recheck immutable identity, current grants, generation and request validity immediately before dispatch. A response from an older connection generation cannot settle a newer request; duplicate and late responses cannot double-release, revive or retarget work.

Bound reconnect attempts and elapsed recovery time using named configuration, capped backoff and jitter, with a typed circuit-open state and an explicit eligible recovery transition. Preserve the negotiated server initialization/capability contract. Do not replay a potentially executed mutation unless the canonical tool idempotency contract and actual remote outcome allow it; otherwise surface unknown outcome.

A request flood while connected or disconnected, oversized inbound framing, slow writer and slow inbound handler produce bounded queue/pending/byte/worker high-water marks and explicit rejection or timeout. Cancellation and control remain responsive within the declared bound. The test proves counters against actual admitted work, not only configured limits.

Preserve canonical tool identity, schema validation, side-effect and idempotency rules, capability intersection, ModelSession/tool_call_id/trace_id correlation and redaction. Prove authorized calls plus missing/revoked/mismatched grants, same-project private resources, cross-account requests and revocation during reconnect. Denial metadata and diagnostics cannot disclose foreign work.

Identify and exercise a real shipped production caller that constructs/adopts this MCP request lifecycle. The inspected baseline verifies constructors in tests and internal gate assembly only. If adoption requires a host file outside this MT, Primary owns the exact integration change and the missing caller remains a named acceptance dependency; library/fixture success is not product acceptance.

Emit scoped Flight Recorder business outcomes for admission rejection, request timeout, cancellation request, transport failure and recovery using existing contracts. Record queue/byte/pending high-water marks, deadline and circuit state as typed internal_diagnostics health metadata. Feed existing Palmistry registration/transport with passive liveness and survivor evidence, without turning Palmistry into a recovery controller or leaking payloads.

Publish the typed backend state/schema and same-change UserManual interface consumed by MT-209 through Primary. Document overloaded/disconnected/expired/circuit-open/unknown states and safe recovery. Backend acceptance proves the published contract, actual production caller and backend diagnostic outputs independently. MT-209 owns native Dev Command Center controls, Argus and no-focus proof, which remain required for WP closure and are not prerequisites for this backend MT PASS. No GUI or manual write authority is granted to this MT.

Independent acceptance exercises the affected real MCP adoption path with flood, disconnect-before-send, disconnect-after-send, failed send, EOF, expiration during backoff, duplicate/late response, stalled inbound handler and recoverable/nonrecoverable reconnect cases. Bind proof to exact source/config/server contract and observed bounds; static or mock proof alone cannot set PASS.

same_project_private_resource_cases: Two accounts in one project cannot discover or cancel each other's private request/process; an explicitly granted shared resource remains usable.
cross_account_negative_cases: An unrelated account and missing, invalid, stale, revoked, mismatched or ambiguous context cannot admit, inspect, cancel or recover another request.
derived_resource_non_widening_cases: Results, error receipts, replay and diagnostic projections retain source scope; late completions cannot widen it.
revocation_and_context_switch_cases: Queued/reconnecting work rechecks current grants before dispatch and rejects revoked work.
A context switch never retargets an accepted request; immutable original identity remains bound through settlement.
remote_saas_mcp_sync_cases: Reconnect preserves server identity, request id, correlation, resource scope and audience-bound delegation; a changed server/grant cannot inherit old authority.
metadata_side_channel_cases: No command, arguments, prompts, tool payloads, tokens, file names or restricted existence metadata enter internal_diagnostics or Palmistry.
Flight Recorder and manual/status lookup enforce scope and retain existing redaction rules.
expected_evidence: Revocation during queue/reconnect and late-response case
No foreign-request cancellation or process disruption

risks: Bounding a queue but leaving producer tasks or pending metadata unbounded moves the memory failure upstream.
A saturated data queue or awaited inbound handler starves cancellation and responses.
Reconnect dispatches expired/revoked work or repeats an already executed non-idempotent tool.
EOF and failed send leak local pending state; local timeout hides unknown remote work.
Library-only tests give a false impression of shipped product coverage.
minimum_controls: Account item/byte/producer/worker/pending capacity before allocation, with reserved control/settlement capacity.
Deadline covers the complete lifetime and is rechecked at actual dispatch; isolate bounded handler work from response/control progress.
Generation and idempotency checks reject stale or unsafe replay; unknown outcome remains explicit.
Exactly-once local terminal accounting plus MT-205 remote-settlement ownership.
Real caller adoption and independent production boundary proof; MT-209 owns GUI evidence.

operator_authority.preservation: Original three-WP scope, source/spec/governance pins, held cases, historical verdicts, independent acceptance and spent run history remain unchanged.

anchors.meaning: Pending request tracking, timeout and notifications/cancelled. Sending the notification is a cancellation request; the claim that it ensures remote CPU work stops requires separately observed settlement.
Current scoped authority, aggregate admission including waiting producers and reclamation, reserved completion/cancellation service, actual retirement and failed-spawn ownership.
Preserve canonical tool identity, schemas, side effects, idempotency, capability intersection, ModelSession correlation, payload sizing and typed error behavior.
Every Handshake-spawned process uses ProcessOwnershipLedger and the existing SandboxAdapter reclaim owner; terminal rows require observed outcomes.

spec_basis.pin_policy: These anchors explain the approved additive work; reading the current bundle does not re-pin original acceptance or rewrite existing MTs.

inspection.source_state: Inspected source only; no runtime, build, test or deployment result created.

source_evidence.finding: Default attempts are unlimited; stable channels and backlog have no request expiry contract.
Dispatcher awaits inbound handlers inline and does not drain pending waiters at EOF. Both request paths insert into pending before a fallible send.
resources/list awaits directly while tools/call has a gate timeout.
Existing timeout test checks notification receipt; it does not prove remote work termination.

context_capsule.caller_evidence: Search found GatedMcpClient constructors in MCP/model-session tests and the internal JsonRpc client construction in mcp/gate.rs. No shipped production MCP constructor caller was verified. Establish the actual production adoption path before claiming end-to-end product acceptance; do not assert a deployed process explosion.

supplied_document.role: Operator-supplied reliability lessons; non-authoritative research input. Only evaluated lessons bound here become task requirements.

official_sources.basis: Parent's inspected official MCP cancellation research; cancellation can race with completion and recipients may be unable to cancel. Preserve request-id and initialization constraints.
Parent's inspected Tokio channel research; bound queues and producer admission rather than moving the unbounded allocation upstream.
Parent's inspected Tokio process research; a kill request and process exit/reap are distinct observations.

research_basis.selected_approach: Extend current typed MCP state and consume existing host owners. Preserve the server contract, privacy and correlation while bounding accepted work and reporting uncertain outcomes.
rejected_options: Treat cancellation notification, dropped future or kill request as remote work settlement.
Add a second reaper/watchdog/permission store or use a static fixture as product adoption proof.
Copy external sample implementations or unverified proposed limits into product authority.

diagnostic_result_policy: Record future per-tier WIRED only after its required observed output is inspected. NOT_APPLICABLE needs a concrete reason; DEFERRED names the unresolved owner/dependency and does not satisfy a required acceptance row. This planned record asserts none of those future outcomes.
